cards.name: The Fool
cards.uprightMeaning: A new chapter is opening. Trust the unknown and step forward with an open heart. The Fool reminds you that every great journey begins with a single, unguarded moment of yes.
cards.reversedMeaning: Hesitation, second-guessing, or a leap taken without thought. Slow down and consider whether this risk is freedom — or escape. Look before you leap.
cards.description: A young figure steps toward a cliff edge, eyes on the sky, a small dog at their heels. They carry a white rose and a knapsack of essentials.

cards.name: The Magician
cards.uprightMeaning: You have all the tools you need at your disposal. Channel intention into action. The Magician is the spark that turns thought into form.
cards.reversedMeaning: Power misused, talent wasted, or someone weaving illusion. Examine where you may be deceiving yourself or being deceived.
cards.description: A figure stands at an altar bearing a wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, one hand pointing to heaven, the other to earth.

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.uprightMeaning: The answer lives in stillness. Listen to the quiet knowing beneath your reasoning mind. There is more here than meets the eye.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're cut off from your inner voice, or hiding something — even from yourself. Step back from the noise and let the truth surface.
cards.description: A robed priestess sits between two pillars, a crescent moon at her feet, a Torah scroll in her lap, a veil of pomegranates behind her.

cards.name: The Empress
cards.uprightMeaning: Lush, generous, and fully present in the body. Something you've nurtured is ready to bloom — a project, a relationship, a self.
cards.reversedMeaning: Care turned into control, or care neglected entirely. Tend to what you have created — including yourself.
cards.description: A crowned figure reclines in a field of wheat, surrounded by lush forest, a scepter in hand, a heart-shaped shield bearing Venus's symbol beside her.

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.uprightMeaning: Order brings peace. Define the rules of your world and lead within them. The Emperor builds the container that allows life to flourish.
cards.reversedMeaning: Control has become coercion, or your foundations are crumbling. Examine where structure has hardened into a cage.
cards.description: A bearded king sits on a stone throne adorned with rams' heads, ankh in one hand and orb in the other, a barren mountain range behind him.

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.uprightMeaning: There is wisdom in the old ways. Seek a teacher, study a tradition, or honor a sacred ritual that grounds you.
cards.reversedMeaning: Tradition no longer serves you. Forge your own path and trust your own counsel — but know what you're stepping away from.
cards.description: A robed pope figure raises one hand in blessing, holding a triple-cross staff, two acolytes kneeling at his feet between two stone pillars.

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.uprightMeaning: A union of opposites — romantic, creative, or moral. A choice approaches that asks you to know what you truly value.
cards.reversedMeaning: Disharmony in a relationship, or a values conflict pulling you in two directions. The choice can no longer be avoided.
cards.description: A naked man and woman stand before an angel emerging from clouds, the Tree of Life behind one and the Tree of Knowledge behind the other.

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.uprightMeaning: Hold the reins. Two opposing forces can be made to pull together when you know where you're going. Victory comes through focused will.
cards.reversedMeaning: You've lost the thread, or you're forcing things by sheer will. Pause and find your true direction before you push on.
cards.description: An armored figure in a stone chariot is pulled by two sphinxes — one black, one white — beneath a starry canopy.

cards.name: Strength
cards.uprightMeaning: Real power is gentle. The lion is not slain but soothed. Whatever you face, meet it with patience and a steady heart.
cards.reversedMeaning: Fear is in the driver's seat. The instinct you've been wrestling with isn't an enemy — listen to what it's trying to tell you.
cards.description: A serene woman gently closes the jaws of a lion, an infinity symbol floating above her head.

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.uprightMeaning: Step back from the noise. The light you need can only be found by lifting your own lantern. Solitude is sacred here.
cards.reversedMeaning: Solitude has soured into isolation. You've been alone with your thoughts long enough — let someone in.
cards.description: A robed elder stands on a snowy mountaintop, lantern in hand, a six-pointed star within the lantern.

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.uprightMeaning: The wheel turns. What was up will come down, what was down will rise. Whatever you're in won't last — adjust accordingly.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're fighting the current. The cycle wants to turn — let it. Resistance is making this harder than it needs to be.
cards.description: A great wheel turns in the sky surrounded by four winged creatures — bull, lion, eagle, angel — with a sphinx atop the wheel.

cards.name: Justice
cards.uprightMeaning: The truth is being weighed. What you've done is coming back to meet you — for better or worse. Honesty is the only way through.
cards.reversedMeaning: Imbalance, evasion, or a wrong yet to be set right. Look at where you're avoiding accountability — yours or someone else's.
cards.description: A crowned figure sits between two pillars, sword raised in one hand, scales held aloft in the other.

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.uprightMeaning: Stop trying to push. The view from this strange angle is the gift. Surrender what you cannot control and a new understanding will arrive.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're stuck and you know it. The pause was meant to teach you something — but you've stopped listening. Find the lesson or move on.
cards.description: A figure hangs upside-down from a T-shaped tree by one foot, hands behind his back, a halo of light around his head.

cards.name: Death
cards.uprightMeaning: Something is ending so something else can begin. This is rarely physical death — it is the death of an old self, a phase, an attachment. Let it go.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're clinging to what's already gone. The ending is happening with or without your consent — make peace with it.
cards.description: A skeletal knight in black armor rides a pale horse beneath a setting sun, a white rose banner in his hand, figures fallen at his feet.

cards.name: Temperance
cards.uprightMeaning: Mix slowly. The right blend of opposing forces is being found. Patience is producing something neither extreme could create alone.
cards.reversedMeaning: Too much of one thing, not enough of the other. You're rushing — or you've stopped tending the mixture entirely.
cards.description: A winged angel pours water between two cups, one foot on land and one in a stream, a rising path leading to a crowned mountain behind.

cards.name: The Devil
cards.uprightMeaning: You are chained, but the chains are loose. Look closely — what feels inescapable is something you could put down. Confront the shadow honestly.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're loosening the grip of something that held you. Power is returning. Don't underestimate the work you've done.
cards.description: A horned, winged figure crouches on a black plinth as a naked man and woman stand chained at his feet — chains loose enough to slip off.

cards.name: The Tower
cards.uprightMeaning: The structure built on a false foundation is coming down. Painful, fast, necessary. What's left standing afterwards is what is real.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're holding the tower up with both hands. The collapse is coming whether you brace for it or not — at least look it in the eye.
cards.description: A tall stone tower is struck by lightning, its crown falling, two figures plummeting from the windows into darkness.

cards.name: The Star
cards.uprightMeaning: After the storm, calm. Let the soft light in. Healing is happening even if you can't see it yet — trust the slow return of hope.
cards.reversedMeaning: Hope feels distant. You've forgotten what you were reaching for. Look up — the light is still there, you've just stopped looking.
cards.description: A naked woman kneels by a pool, pouring water from two vessels — one onto the land, one into the water — beneath a great star and seven smaller ones.

cards.name: The Moon
cards.uprightMeaning: Things are not as they appear. Trust the body more than the eye. There is something you sense but can't name yet — give it time.
cards.reversedMeaning: The fog is lifting. What looked monstrous is being seen for what it really is. Clarity returns slowly but surely.
cards.description: A full moon shines over a winding path between two towers, a wolf and a dog howling below, a crayfish emerging from a pool.

cards.name: The Sun
cards.uprightMeaning: Yes. Wholeheartedly, plainly, brightly: yes. The Sun is unambiguous good news — the warmth is real and you've earned it.
cards.reversedMeaning: The sun is still there but you can't quite feel it. A small obstacle, a small fog. It will pass — keep going.
cards.description: A naked child rides a white horse beneath a radiant sun, sunflowers blooming behind a stone wall.

cards.name: Judgement
cards.uprightMeaning: A call you can't unhear. The past is being reviewed and a new chapter is opening in response. Step out of the coffin and into your life.
cards.reversedMeaning: You hear the call but won't answer. Or you're judging yourself so harshly you can't move. Forgive what needs forgiving.
cards.description: An angel blows a great trumpet from the clouds as the dead rise from coffins below, arms raised toward the sound.

cards.name: The World
cards.uprightMeaning: The journey is complete. You have all the parts of yourself in the same room for the first time. Stand in this moment fully.
cards.reversedMeaning: Almost — but not quite. One last piece of the puzzle is unaccounted for. Resist the urge to call it done.
cards.description: A dancing figure draped in violet floats inside a wreath of laurels, a wand in each hand, the four creatures of the Wheel surrounding her.

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: A creative or passionate idea has arrived, alive in your hands. Don't overthink it — feed it kindling.
cards.reversedMeaning: The match keeps going out. Either it's not the right time, or you're hesitating because you sense something is off.
cards.description: A hand emerges from a cloud holding a sprouting wooden staff, leaves still attached.

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: You stand at the edge of your own kingdom looking out. The world is wider than you thought — it's time to plan the journey.
cards.reversedMeaning: You can see the road but you won't take the first step. What is keeping you on the parapet?
cards.description: A figure in red holds a globe and gazes out over the sea from a castle wall, two staffs nearby.

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Your ships are out on the water. The first wave of effort has paid off — now you wait, watch, and prepare for what returns.
cards.reversedMeaning: Plans set in motion are returning empty-handed, or returning slower than expected. Recheck the assumptions.
cards.description: A figure stands on a cliff, three tall staffs around him, watching ships sail in the distance.

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: A milestone reached. A wedding, a homecoming, a victory worth pausing for. Rest in this happiness — it's earned.
cards.reversedMeaning: The celebration is delayed or strained. Something at home is unsteady — not ruined, but worth tending to.
cards.description: Four staffs hold up a flowered canopy as two figures dance with bouquets in hand, a castle in the background.

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Everyone is talking, no one is listening. A messy clash of wills — energizing if you stay in it, exhausting if you don't.
cards.reversedMeaning: The shouting has stopped. People are finding common ground, or you've found a way to step out of the fray.
cards.description: Five young men brandish staffs in a chaotic mock-battle, no one clearly winning.

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Public recognition for real work done. Take the bow. The crowd's approval is welcome, but it's the inner satisfaction that lasts.
cards.reversedMeaning: The applause didn't come — or it came but rang hollow. Check whose validation you were chasing.
cards.description: A laurel-crowned rider on a white horse, a wreath on his staff, a procession behind him.

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Hold the high ground. The challenges are real but so is your right to be where you are. Keep your stance.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're tired. The defending has gone on too long and the cost is climbing. Reassess what's worth keeping.
cards.description: A figure on a hilltop holds off six staffs reaching up at him from below.

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Things are moving fast. News, travel, a sudden burst of progress. Ride the momentum — it won't last forever, but while it does, fly.
cards.reversedMeaning: What was racing has stalled. Crossed signals, missed messages. Pause before you push.
cards.description: Eight staffs fly through the air in parallel formation across a clear sky.

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: You're battered but you're still standing. One more push. The finish line is close enough to see.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're treating allies like enemies. The wariness has metastasized — drop your guard for someone trustworthy.
cards.description: A bandaged figure leans on his staff, eight others standing behind him like a fence.

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: You're carrying more than you signed up for. The end is in sight, but the load is real — set some of it down before you break.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're either putting it down at last — or you've broken under it. Either way, something is being released.
cards.description: A bent figure trudges toward a town carrying ten staffs in his arms, his face hidden by the load.

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: A young, eager spirit. A fresh idea wants to be tried out. Don't worry yet about whether it's serious — let it run.
cards.reversedMeaning: Lots of starts, no follow-through. Or someone full of bluster who never quite delivers.
cards.description: A youth in patterned tunic stands in a desert plain, gazing up at a sprouting wooden staff.

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Charging in, full speed. Bold, reckless, unforgettable. Use the energy while it's hot.
cards.reversedMeaning: All gas, no brakes — and the wreck is overdue. Or the engine has finally cooled and you don't know what to do without the chase.
cards.description: A knight in flame-patterned armor rides a rearing horse across a desert, a sprouting staff in hand.

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: Warm, vivid, unapologetically herself. She gets things done by being who she is. Let that energy in — or be that energy.
cards.reversedMeaning: The shine is being performed instead of lived. Or insecurity is leaking out as control.
cards.description: A regal woman sits on a stone throne adorned with lions, sunflower in hand, a black cat at her feet.

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.uprightMeaning: A leader who inspires. He sees the horizon and knows how to move others toward it. Step into that role, or follow someone who has.
cards.reversedMeaning: Vision without listening becomes tyranny. Or a leader running on ego instead of clarity.
cards.description: A crowned king sits on a throne adorned with lions and salamanders, holding a sprouting staff.

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: A new emotional current is opening. Love, compassion, creativity flowing in. Let yourself be filled.
cards.reversedMeaning: Something has dammed the flow — old grief, fear, or simply your own walls. The cup wants to be poured into.
cards.description: A hand holds out a chalice from a cloud, water spilling over its sides, a dove with a host descending toward it.

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: A meeting of equals. A real partnership in love or work. The exchange feels effortless — protect that.
cards.reversedMeaning: The give-and-take has tilted. One person is pouring, the other receiving without returning — or vice versa.
cards.description: Two figures raise cups to each other beneath a winged lion's head and caduceus emblem.

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Your people. The chosen family, the friends, the circle. Lean into the joy of being surrounded by those who get you.
cards.reversedMeaning: The party has soured into something less wholesome — gossip, excess, or feeling alone in a crowd.
cards.description: Three women dance in a circle, cups raised, fruit at their feet.

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: An offer is being held out and you're not noticing. Or you've grown numb to what's in front of you. Look up.
cards.reversedMeaning: Whatever fog had settled is lifting. You're reaching out again — for connection, for what you'd been ignoring.
cards.description: A figure sits beneath a tree, arms crossed, looking down at three cups while a fourth is offered from a cloud.

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Three cups are spilled, but two still stand. Grief is real — and there is still something here for you. Turn around.
cards.reversedMeaning: The grief is loosening its grip. You're starting to see what survived the loss, and to forgive what couldn't.
cards.description: A cloaked figure stares down at three spilled cups, two upright cups behind him, a river and bridge beyond.

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: A return of something gentle from the past. An old friend, a memory, a softness you'd forgotten you had.
cards.reversedMeaning: Nostalgia has become a hiding place. Or you're outgrowing what used to comfort you. Both can be true.
cards.description: A child hands a cup full of flowers to a smaller child in a sunlit village courtyard.

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Too many tempting visions, none of them quite real. Don't pick from the fog — wait until something concrete appears.
cards.reversedMeaning: The mist is clearing. You can finally see which of these dreams was real and which was just glitter.
cards.description: A figure in silhouette gazes at seven cups floating in clouds, each filled with a different image — a face, a serpent, a castle, a crown.

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: You've outgrown what you built. Quietly, without drama, you're walking toward something that has more meaning. Let yourself go.
cards.reversedMeaning: You almost left, then turned back. Either it wasn't time, or you flinched. Be honest with yourself about which.
cards.description: A cloaked figure walks away from eight stacked cups beneath a mournful moon.

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: The 'wish card.' What you've been wanting is yours. Enjoy it without apology.
cards.reversedMeaning: You got what you wanted and it didn't fill what you thought it would. Or the satisfaction is performative. Look deeper.
cards.description: A satisfied man sits with arms crossed in front of nine cups arranged in an arc.

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: The kind of happiness you can rest in. Family, partnership, a life that is whole. This is rare — appreciate it openly.
cards.reversedMeaning: The picture-perfect frame doesn't match the inside of the home. Something needs honest attention — repair what can be repaired.
cards.description: A couple stands with two children beneath a rainbow of ten cups, a small home in the distance.

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Something tender is rising — a creative impulse, a soft message, an unguarded feeling. Make space for it.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're sulking, or someone near you is. The feeling is real but the expression is stuck.
cards.description: A youth in a flowered tunic stands by the sea, looking surprised at a fish appearing in his cup.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: An offer from the heart — a date, an invitation, a vulnerable gesture. Receive it on its own terms.
cards.reversedMeaning: All poetry, no follow-through. Or the romance was a story you told yourself. Step out of the dream.
cards.description: A knight in winged helm rides a quiet white horse, a chalice held out before him.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: The deep listener. Holds others' feelings without losing herself. Let yourself be cared for, or be that care for someone else.
cards.reversedMeaning: Empathy has overflowed into self-loss. Or someone is using their feelings to control the room.
cards.description: A robed queen sits on a throne by the sea, gazing into an ornate covered cup.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.uprightMeaning: Steady in turbulent water. Holds his own emotions and others' without being swept under. Look for this in yourself.
cards.reversedMeaning: Calm on the surface, churn below. The cost of holding it all in is showing somewhere.
cards.description: A crowned king sits on a stone throne in the middle of a rough sea, holding a chalice and scepter.

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: A clarifying thought has cut through the fog. The truth, in a single line. Use it cleanly.
cards.reversedMeaning: The blade is being used carelessly — words that wound, truths weaponized. Or the clarity hasn't yet arrived.
cards.description: A hand emerges from a cloud holding an upright sword crowned with a wreath.

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: You're avoiding the choice by refusing to look. The blindfold is a defense — and it isn't working anymore.
cards.reversedMeaning: The blindfold comes off. The decision can finally be made because you've allowed yourself to see.
cards.description: A blindfolded figure sits with two swords crossed at her chest, the moon behind her over a calm sea.

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: A clean, sharp grief. The pain is real and worth feeling. Don't rush past it — but don't make a home in it either.
cards.reversedMeaning: The wounds are closing. Forgiveness, of self or others, is becoming possible.
cards.description: Three swords pierce a heart hovering against grey rain clouds.

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Lie down. Take the sabbath. The work will be there when you return — and it will go better for the rest.
cards.reversedMeaning: You can't slow down, or rest itself feels unsafe. Notice what you're afraid will happen if you stop.
cards.description: A knight lies in repose on a stone tomb, three swords on the wall above him, one beneath.

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: You can win this fight — but at what cost. The smirk on the victor's face won't last. Ask if winning is worth the bridges burned.
cards.reversedMeaning: Coming back from a fight you wish you hadn't had. Apology, repair, choosing peace over rightness.
cards.description: A smug figure gathers fallen swords as two defeated figures walk away beneath a stormy sky.

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Quietly leaving rough seas behind. The new place isn't bright yet but it is calmer. Trust the crossing.
cards.reversedMeaning: Trying to leave with one foot still on the dock. Or being pulled back by what you haven't finished.
cards.description: A ferryman poles a boat carrying a cloaked figure and child across calm water, six swords standing in the boat's prow.

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Sneaking off with what you couldn't get openly. Sometimes clever, often dishonest. Watch where this puts you.
cards.reversedMeaning: What was hidden is being seen. Either by you, finally, or by someone else. Either way, the secret is up.
cards.description: A figure tiptoes away from a camp clutching five swords, two left behind in the ground.

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: You feel trapped. The ropes are looser than you think. Look at how the situation could move if you stopped assuming it can't.
cards.reversedMeaning: The ropes are coming off. You're seeing the choices you couldn't see before.
cards.description: A bound and blindfolded woman stands in a marsh, surrounded by eight swords planted in the mud.

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: The 3am card. The thoughts circling are louder than the truth. The night is the hardest part — daylight will reframe most of this.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're stepping out of a long anxious spiral. The fear is still there but smaller now. Be gentle.
cards.description: A figure sits up in bed, head in hands, nine swords mounted on the wall behind her.

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: It's already done. The dramatic worst has passed. From here, the only direction is up — and the dawn is on the horizon.
cards.reversedMeaning: Slow rise from the floor. You're not all the way up yet, but you're not where you were.
cards.description: A figure lies face-down with ten swords in his back, dawn breaking on the horizon.

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Sharp, curious, ready to ask the inconvenient question. Use the energy to learn — not to spar.
cards.reversedMeaning: The sharpness has slid into snark. Or someone is gossiping behind your back.
cards.description: A youth stands on a windswept hill, holding a sword aloft as if testing the air.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Fast and direct. Cuts to the point. Useful in the right battle — exhausting in the wrong one.
cards.reversedMeaning: All charge, no thought. Wreckage in his wake. Pause and assess what's been damaged.
cards.description: A knight charges across a field, sword raised, his horse's mane streaming in the wind.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: Clear-eyed. Doesn't sugar-coat, doesn't lie. The friend who tells you the truth even when it's hard. Be that — or seek that.
cards.reversedMeaning: Truthfulness has hardened into cruelty. Or grief has turned the sharp mind cold.
cards.description: A queen sits on a throne above the clouds, sword raised vertically in one hand, the other beckoning.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.uprightMeaning: The fair-minded judge. Acts on principle and reasoning, not mood. Bring this energy to the situation.
cards.reversedMeaning: Logic without empathy becomes cruelty. Authority without ethics becomes tyranny. Be careful.
cards.description: A crowned king sits on a stone throne, sword held upright, butterflies and clouds in the carving behind him.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: A real, tangible opportunity has arrived. A job, a windfall, a foundation to build on. Take it seriously.
cards.reversedMeaning: The chance is there but hesitation, fear, or scarcity-thinking is keeping your hands closed.
cards.description: A hand from a cloud holds a single golden pentacle above a flowering garden.

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: You're juggling well — for now. Stay nimble, stay present. The rhythm works as long as you don't try to add a third.
cards.reversedMeaning: Something is going to drop. Either set one of these down on purpose, or let it fall on its own.
cards.description: A man dances while juggling two pentacles linked by an infinity-shaped ribbon, ships rising and falling on waves behind him.

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Skilled people working together on something worth building. Each is needed. Recognize the contribution.
cards.reversedMeaning: The collaboration isn't working — egos, mismatched skills, unclear roles. Realign or let go.
cards.description: A craftsman works on a cathedral while two robed figures consult plans nearby.

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: You've got it and you're not letting go. Reasonable in moderation — pathological if it becomes your only stance toward life.
cards.reversedMeaning: The hands are starting to open. Generosity, sharing, the relief of trusting that more will come.
cards.description: A crowned figure clutches a pentacle to his chest, one beneath each foot, one balanced on his head.

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Hard times — and there is help nearby that you may not be seeing. Look up. Ask. The lit window is closer than it looks.
cards.reversedMeaning: You're walking back into the warmth. Help is being asked for and received. The hard part is loosening.
cards.description: Two ragged figures trudge through snow past a stained-glass church window, unaware of the warmth inside.

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Resources flowing where they're needed. You're either giving or receiving — both with grace. Note the scales in his hand.
cards.reversedMeaning: The 'gift' has strings. Or you're stuck in a one-sided dynamic. Look for the imbalance.
cards.description: A wealthy merchant weighs gold on a scale and drops coins into the hands of two beggars at his feet.

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: You've planted, you've watered. Now you wait. Resist the urge to dig up the seeds to see if they're growing — they are.
cards.reversedMeaning: Either the patience has cracked, or the effort wasn't producing what you hoped. Be honest about which.
cards.description: A farmer leans on his hoe, surveying a vine heavy with seven pentacles.

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: The quiet joy of getting good at something. Repetition, refinement, attention. Stay with it.
cards.reversedMeaning: Effort without joy has become drudgery, or perfectionism is making you rework what was already good.
cards.description: A craftsman hammers a pentacle at his bench, seven completed ones displayed on a post beside him.

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: You did this. The garden, the house, the life. Stand in it. The pleasure of having earned what you have is real and clean.
cards.reversedMeaning: The garden is beautiful but you're alone in it. Or the wealth is more performance than substance.
cards.description: A finely dressed woman stands in a lush vineyard, a hooded falcon on her gloved hand.

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Generations woven together. The kind of wealth that includes children, dogs, family stories, a home with depth. Preserve it.
cards.reversedMeaning: Disputes over inheritance, family rifts, or the legacy not landing where it should.
cards.description: An old patriarch sits with his dogs while a young couple and child stand nearby, ten pentacles arranged across the scene.

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Earnest, focused, willing to start at the bottom. A new project or skill that you're ready to learn the right way.
cards.reversedMeaning: All study, no practice. Or no study at all and you're winging it. Either way, address it directly.
cards.description: A youth stands in a green field, holding a single pentacle aloft and gazing at it.

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Slow and steady. Boring, beautiful, effective. The work gets done because he shows up every day.
cards.reversedMeaning: Steady has tipped into stuck. The same routine, no growth. Stir something up.
cards.description: A knight in dark armor sits motionless on a heavy horse, holding a pentacle, fields stretching behind him.

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Generous, grounded, skilled at making places feel like home. Tends to the body and the practical world. Embody this.
cards.reversedMeaning: Tending everyone but yourself. The well runs dry if you don't refill it.
cards.description: A queen sits in a flowering garden, a pentacle in her lap, a rabbit nearby.

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.uprightMeaning: Built well, holds well. Money, business, foundations all in good order. Trust the structure he has made.
cards.reversedMeaning: Wealth has hardened into greed, or the king has stopped growing because he's protecting what he has.
cards.description: A robed king sits on a throne carved with bulls, surrounded by grapes and pentacles, his castle behind him.
